propositions: BindingStore embeds dispersed lifecycle logic (identity transitions, pending/confirmed state, re-keying, comments, tombstones, retirement) that should be consolidated into a dedicated policy owner
Production rich-text emission mutates dictionaries through shallow all_bindings() query, bypassing future policy seams and requiring a narrow, supported mutation operation
Lifecycle policy must preserve at-most-one identity invariant and remove stale reverse entries only via targeted single-key pops, never sweeping cleanup or abort-on-ambiguity
The public BindingStore facade must retain all existing method signatures and shallow all_bindings() semantics while delegating cohesive lifecycle decisions to a private policy module

A new narrow operation (note_rich_emit or equivalent) must replace direct dictionary mutation as the supported production seam for rich-emission state updates while preserving hash/counter behavior and missing-binding fail-open semantics

All existing failure modes (confirmed 404 grace/reset, moved-key repair, retired corruption fail-open, live corruption fail-closed, append-only comment identity, tombstone suppression, unretire) must remain unchanged; no caller receives direct repository write access
